data.title: Democrats seek records on Nvidia sway in Megaspeed probe
data.description:
• Democratic lawmakers have reportedly opened a probe into what influence Nvidia (NVDA) was able to wield over a U.S. Commerce Department investigation of ​cloud company Megaspeed for possible illegal diversion of chips to China.
  • In the November 19 letter to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, the House Democrats said they wanted to know "whether the department allowed a major American corporation that is financially and ​personally linked to the Trump administration to interfere with enforcement activity," according ‌to a letter reviewed by Reuters.
  • Megaspeed, an Nvidia partner that operates data centers, has been under US investigation for two years, the departments of Commerce and Justice said this week. They said Commerce investigators requested records from Nvidia ​in May 2025 about sales to the company and, with Singaporean authorities, conducted an ​on-site inspection in June 2025 at Megaspeed and interviewed Alice Huang, according to the report.
  • In August 2025, Nvidia contacted Commerce employees directly and ‌requested ⁠a meeting with one of them, a Commerce official told Reuters, referring to the investigators. Nvidia told them Commerce Under Secretary Jeffrey Kessler said the company could communicate with the employees.
  • "The American public and Congress deserve a full accounting of what happened, " US Representatives Gregory ​Meeks, ranking member ​of the House ⁠Committee on Foreign Affairs, and Sydney Kamlager-Dove of California wrote in the letter, which requested answers and relevant documents by December 1.
  • Separately, California Attorney General Rob Bonta served an investigative subpoena on Nvidia (NVDA) related to former CEO Jensen Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese operative.

data.title: US lawmakers near deal to ban Chinese cars, with potential exemption for Mercedes: report
data.description:
U.S. lawmakers are nearing an agreement on legislation to ban Chinese cars from the domestic market, with last-minute negotiations focused partly on protecting Mercedes-Benz (MBGAF), which is nearly 20% owned by Chinese entities, Bloomberg reported, citing people familiar with the matter.

Republican and Democratic lawmakers from auto-producing states aim to send the bill to President Donald Trump by year-end. The measure would further restrict Chinese automakers such as BYD (BYDDY) (BYDDF) and Geely (GELYF) from accessing the lucrative US market, which is already largely closed to them by tariffs and restrictions on Chinese vehicle technology.

Republican Senator Bernie Moreno briefed automaker representatives Wednesday on proposed changes to earlier legislation targeting Chinese connected vehicles. The revisions include provisions that could shield Mercedes from an outright ban, the people said.

Automakers were broadly supportive of the proposed changes, although a Mercedes representative raised reservations. Negotiations remain ongoing, with lawmakers hoping to pass the measure before the next Congress begins in January.

“We continue to meet with all stakeholders who have a shared interest in ensuring this important legislation becomes law in this Congress,” Mercedes said.

An earlier bill advanced by a Senate panel would have barred manufacturers more than 15% owned by Chinese entities from selling vehicles equipped with data-transmitting technology. Mercedes has lobbied for changes to the proposal. China's state-owned BAIC Motor owns nearly 10% of the German automaker, while Geely founder Li Shufu holds nearly another 10%.

Provisions under discussion include relaxing restrictions for companies with passive ownership stakes that lack voting rights, as well as ways to structure and verify such exemptions, the people said.

Republican Senator Katie Britt of Alabama, where Mercedes operates a major SUV production facility, said she had worked on the legislation with Moreno and believed both the automaker and the state would be protected.

“We understand that there will be some adjustments that have to be made, but feel good about Mercedes continuing to be able to thrive in our state and across the country,” she said.

US automakers such as General Motors (GM), Ford (F) and Tesla (TSLA) could benefit from reduced competition if Chinese automakers are further restricted from accessing the US market.

data.title: Gold slide deepens as market anxiety overtakes real-rate pressures
data.description:
Gold prices are tumbling as the Federal Reserve's aggressive rate-hiking cycle sparks a "fear factor" in markets that may be triggering a deleveraging wave, according to strategist Robin J. Brooks.

The unusual price action this week in precious metals comes alongside a sharp rise in the dollar against emerging markets, which Brooks describes as "usually an indication of deleveraging kicking in."

The Fed's hawkish stance is driving real Treasury yields to their highest levels in over two decades, creating significant headwinds for gold, the strategist explained. While falling oil prices have provided some support for the precious metal, that effect has faded now that Brent crude has settled in the low $90s per barrel. "The rise in real rates is certainly weighing on gold, but that effect is minor," Brooks said, noting that the more significant driver is market anxiety.

Non-linear moves in the dollar, gold, and copper are emerging even as real rates and oil prices have recently stabilized, suggesting that "stuff is breaking," according to Brooks.

His regression analysis of gold's daily price movements shows that the "fear factor" has been building since Fed Governor Waller began discussing 50-basis-point rate hikes ahead of last week's inflation data. "The fact that real rates in recent days stopped rising, even as gold has continued to fall, suggests that a fear factor is at play," he said.

Brooks warned that the Fed's hawkishness could prove self-defeating and may cause a market "accident." "Once deleveraging starts, unpredictable things can happen," he cautioned, adding that geopolitical risks involving Iran could further complicate the outlook.

The strategist called on Fed Chair Warsh to provide clearer forward guidance, arguing that internal squabbling should not "hold the US economy hostage."

data.title: AM Need to Know: Alibaba faces Megaspeed lawsuit, Nvidia eyes AI acquisition & more
data.description:
U.S. stock futures fell early Friday as investors assessed the fallout from Wall Street's sharp selloff in the previous session, when major indexes tumbled more than 2% each.

Now, here are four news stories that broke overnight to watch out for:

Alibaba sued by shareholders over Megaspeed ties amid Nvidia spy scandal: Alibaba (BABA)  faces a proposed class action lawsuit filed Thursday in Manhattan federal court, with shareholders alleging the Chinese e-commerce giant misled them by concealing connections to Megaspeed, a Singaporean company suspected of helping Beijing access advanced Nvidia AI chips. The complaint claims Alibaba knowingly understated in its 2024, 2025, and 2026 annual reports the risks that actual or suspected export control violations could harm its business. Shareholders cited Alibaba's relationship with Megaspeed, whose executive Alice Huang had a relationship with former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and reportedly helped move about 240,000 H100, H200, and A100 chips into China. 

SpaceX sells $32 billion in off-balance-sheet AI chip debt above 8% yield: SpaceX (SPCX) sold $32 billion of bonds Thursday to fund its  purchase of artificial intelligence chips, in a transaction that may serve as a model for similar financings to come. The debt offering was designed to keep the borrowing off SpaceX's balance sheet and is part of a more than $40 billion financing that also includes bank loans. Goldman Sachs and Apollo Global Management ran the transaction, which will allow SpaceX to buy Nvidia chips that the company will lease for about five years.

Nvidia in advanced talks to buy AI startup Inception for over $500 million: Nvidia (NVDA)  is in advanced discussions to  acquire Inception, a two-year-old AI startup developing diffusion-based large language models, in a deal valued at more than $500 million. The transaction would bring Inception's three co-founders—Stefano Ermon, Aditya Grover, and Volodymyr Kuleshov—into Nvidia full-time. Based in the San Francisco Bay Area, Inception has more than 30 employees and previously raised $50 million from investors including Menlo Ventures, M12, Mayfield, and Nvidia. 

U.K. retail sales volumes increase 2.3% Y/Y in October, topping estimates: U.K. retail sales volumes  rose 0.7% month-over-month in October, beating economists' expectations for no growth, according to data released by the Office for National Statistics. The increase followed a 0.4% decline in September. On a year-over-year basis, retail sales volumes rose 2.3%, accelerating from 0.8% growth in the previous month and exceeding consensus estimates of 1.7%. The stronger-than-expected reading points to an improvement in consumer spending, with both monthly and annual retail sales growth exceeding market forecasts.

data.title: AI selloff: Taiwan's benchmark index posts worst week since 1991
data.description:
Taiwan's stock market extended losses on Friday, capping off its worst week in decades, tracking the global tech selloff as Anthropic's (ANT) IPO failed to quell concerns over the AI trade.

The tech-heavy TAIEX Index (TWSE) closed down 6.6% on Friday. It ended the week 17.5% lower, notching its worst week since 1991.

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSM), which accounts for over 40% of TAIEX's weighting, slid nearly 5%.

Anthopic (ANT) made its record stock market debut on Thursday, and while shares initially soared amid opening-day euphoria, they pared gains later in the session. The stock is down 6% premarket on Friday.

"The message is becoming clearer: investors still believe in AI's potential, but are increasingly questioning how much they should pay for that potential," said Charu Chanana, chief investment strategist, Saxo.

Anthropic's (ANT) IPO "arrives at a moment when strong AI earnings and fundraising announcements are no longer enough to lift the entire sector," she added.

Recent tech outages and Nvidia's (NVDA) leadership turmoil had already dented sentiment prior to Anthropic's (ANT) IPO.

TAIEX (TWSE) also saw a steep selloff on Monday, when the index fell 6%. Barclays said the rout was primarily driven by forced selling by retail investors.

While Taiwan's market regulator recently tightened curbs on short selling, the move hasn't done much to help stabilize the market.

"Limiting short-selling activity does not eliminate underlying bearish sentiment or selling pressure from investors reducing existing long exposure," Matthew Unterman, head of research at S3 Partners, told Bloomberg News.

data.title: Trump administration signed off nearly 900,000 Nvidia, AMD AI chips for China in six months
Biggest stock movers Friday: ANT, INTU, and more
data.description:
Stock futures edged lower Friday morning as Anthropic's record-breaking IPO failed to ease broader valuation and rate-hike fears weighing on the AI trade. 

Here are some of Friday's biggest stock movers:

Biggest stock gainers

  • Gap (GAP) +3% - Shares rose after the retailer reported mixed Q3 results, with adjusted EPS of $0.82 beating the $0.78 consensus and comparable sales outperforming expectations at Old Navy and Gap, offsetting continued weakness at Athleta and Banana Republic. Comparable sales declined 15% at Athleta and 3% at Banana Republic, missing expectations for declines of 11% and growth of 2.45%, respectively. GAAP EPS increased 39% to $0.86, helped by IEEPA tariff refunds, which also supported operating margin expansion to 9.9% from a year earlier. However, Gap lowered its FY2026 outlook, now expecting adjusted EPS of $2.29–$2.34 vs. its prior $2.35–$2.45 range and the $2.40 consensus, while forecasting flat net sales of approximately $15.4B. The company also named Ashley Kechter, formerly global president of Vuori and Fabletics, as Athleta's new president and CEO, effective December 14.

Biggest stock losers

  • Intuit (INTU) -10% - Shares plunged despite FQ1 results topping expectations, as the fintech lowered its full-year revenue outlook on weaker-than-expected Credit Karma growth and issued a softer-than-anticipated Q2 forecast. Non-GAAP EPS rose 56% Y/Y to $2.91, beating the $2.64 consensus, while revenue increased 12% to $4.4B, above the $4.31B estimate. However, Intuit cut its FY2027 revenue outlook from $23.28B–$23.51B previously to $23.08B–$23.37B, citing slower consumer demand and revised Credit Karma growth expectations of 3%–7%, down from 11%–13%, while maintaining its adjusted EPS outlook of $22.88–$23.12. Q2 revenue is forecast at $4.93B–$4.95B, below the $5.11B consensus, while adjusted EPS guidance of $3.17–$3.22 also fell short of the $3.73 estimate. Separately, Intuit agreed to sell Mailchimp to Bending Spoons for approximately $3.68B, comprising $3.31B in cash and $368M in stock, with the transaction expected to close in early 2027.
  • Anthropic (ANT) -6% - Shares fell for a second consecutive trading session as a broader market selloff and concerns over AI-sector valuations weighed on sentiment following the company’s record-setting IPO. The stock dropped to $91.25 in early trading, compared with Thursday’s close of $97.17, but remained above its $83 IPO price after jumping 17% in its debut. Anthropic’s $107.3B IPO attracted demand for seven times the shares on offer, with more than half of institutional investors reportedly receiving no allocation, underscoring the strong investor appetite behind its debut.

data.title: Guardforce AI to implement 1-for-40 reverse share split
data.description:
Guardforce AI (GFAI) said it will implement a 1-for-40 reverse share split, with its Class A ordinary shares expected to begin trading on a split-adjusted basis on the Nasdaq Capital Market at the open on Nov. 24.

The reverse split will reduce the number of issued and outstanding ordinary shares from ~31.9M to ~799,233, subject to adjustment for the rounding up of fractional entitlements described below.

The split, approved by the company's board and shareholders, became effective Nov. 11 following registration with the Cayman Islands Registrar of Companies. The company also completed a related capital reduction, share subdivision, and re-designation of its share capital into Class A and Class B ordinary shares.

The Class A shares will replace the existing ordinary shares, continue trading under the “GFAI” ticker.

GFAI shares fell 7.5% premarket.

data.title: Boston Scientific prices debt offerings
data.description:
• Boston Scientific (BSX) priced a public offering of $3B in U.S. dollar-denominated senior notes across four tranches, with maturities ranging from 2029 to 2036.
  • Separately, the company's indirect wholly owned finance subsidiary, American Medical Systems Europe B.V., priced a €4.25B public offering of euro-denominated notes across six tranches, with maturities ranging from 2028 to 2046. The euro notes will be fully and unconditionally guaranteed by Boston Scientific.
  • The offerings are being made pursuant to a registration statement filed with the SEC and are expected to close on Dec. 1, 2026, subject to customary closing conditions.
